doc.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Music of the 1980s and Jazz Nerds
summary: He saw a return to acoustic music in the 1980s; Jason's blog on jazz nerds.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What about – we talked about the music of the ’70s. What happens to the music in the ’80s?

I think the highlight of the music in the ’80s was that it started to return to more acoustic music, not overwhelmingly so, but there started to be more attention being paid to some of the few giants that were still around. That too is kind of close, to be emphatic about it, because the decades don’t break down evenly. They’re good for some things. Like, I would listen to Jason talk about various periods, and it would break down into decades. He’d talk the ’80s and the ’70s, and then in the ’90s. All that’s left me behind. I don’t know these people. For the most part, I’m not really sure how to describe ’80s at all. Did Jason talk to you about Jazz Nerds International?
No, he didn’t talk about that.

That’s interesting. I’m surprised, because he’s got a blog where he wrote Jazz Nerds. He talks about jazz musicians who get stuck in a period and refuse to go back and listen to anything earlier than whatever – wherever they are. There’s more to it than that. He wrote it out.
